newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: World refined copper output up 7 pct in Jan-Aug 96.
newsitem.headline: World refined copper output up 7 pct in Jan-Aug 96.

text.p: World refined copper consumption was up by one percent in the first eight months of 1996 compared with the same 1995 period, while refined production was nearly seven percent higher, the International Copper Study Group (ICSG) said on Monday.
Mine production was 7.5 percent higher in the first eight months of 1996 compared with the same year-ago period, the Lisbon-based ICSG said in a statement.
The four-week world refined copper consumption rate for the first eight months of 1996 was 929,000 tonnes, compared with 923,000 in the same period of 1995.
Refined stocks on the LME and COMEX metal exchanges were 295,600 tonnes at the end of August.
Supply/demand calculations indicated an estimated deficit of about 32,000 tonnes for the first half of 1996, but for the eight-month period there was a surplus of about 76,000 tonnes.
The average LME spot price for July 1996 was $1,984 per tonne, while for August it was higher at $2,008 and in September lower at $1,941 per tonne.
World refined copper consumption and supply trends, 1995-96
(1) = Refined stocks include those held in the exchanges, producers, consumers, merchants and governments in western economies.
(2) = Surplus or deficit is calculated using total refined production minus refined consumption.
